column1: # C28 question 4 at the `textRegionMask` seam, DECOMPOSED BY LAYER — 2026-08-22.
# ⛔ **THE INSTRUMENT THAT PRODUCED THIS FILE IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY AND WILL NOT BE.** It is a
# stranded attempt at the same measurement `WIDEN-STENCIL-2026-08-22.tsv` publishes, from the same base
# commit (`6c154ca`) about two and a half hours earlier, and the seam it used was rejected on 2026-08-22
# — see C28's `#### The same price without the collar`. Both runs union the accepted line groups'
# **bounding rects** into `region`; the ONE difference is that the landed route hands `mrcLayers` a
# `SearchableWriter.BoundingBox` per group and therefore pays `Flattener.mrcBoxPadding`'s 25% collar,
# while this one wrote the same rects straight into the region through a
# `Flattener.textRegionWideningOverride` closure that is not on `main`. So this file prices the collar
# and nothing else. ⚠️ It is NOT an independent implementation: same tool, same `mrcLayers`,
# `textRegionMask`, `fillHoles`, JBIG2 and JPEG, same shape term — one step different.
# The seam's source survives outside the tree as
# `$STATE/rescue/REJECTED-not-on-main-vo-20260822-014509-85956.patch.bak`.
# Kept for four things the landed instrument's columns cannot say, none of them re-derivable from
# anything committed:
#   * the byte delta split into STENCIL / BACKGROUND / FOREGROUND rather than stencil-versus-the-rest;
#   * `MRCLayers.shrunkAsAllText` and `MRCLayers.backgroundWidth` read back from production, where the
#     landed run infers the all-text verdict from two strings — the free control its own review said it
#     left on the table;
#   * `MRCLayers.inkOutsideText` read back from production, against the landed run's recomputation of it;
#   * what the 25% collar costs, in published bytes and in admitted stencil ink.
# One row per page, 26 pages. `arm`: sub73 = one of the 16 sub-bar pages the shape term fires on
# (`SHAPETERM-73-2026-08-21.tsv`, lineN >= 1); pic = one of the 6 picture pages it fires on
# (`SHAPETERM-PICTURES-2026-08-21.tsv`); ctl73 / ctlpic = a page it does NOT fire on, where the widening
# adds nothing and the two publications must therefore be byte-identical. `label`/`kind` are carried
# from those two files. ⚠️ The arm names differ from `WIDEN-STENCIL`'s `subbar`/`picture`, which pool
# the controls into the two arms — compare on `document` + `page`, never on `arm`.
# ⚠️ `wAdd` is the rect's contribution OUTSIDE the shipped region, so it is not the accepted pixels:
# over the 22 firing rows it is **1.90x to 12.94x** `linePx`. That inflation is paid by BOTH routes and
# priced by neither — the collar sits on top of it.
# CONTROLS, all re-run 2026-08-22 against the committed files rather than taken on trust:
#   * `shipTot` equals `SHAPETERM-BYTES-2026-08-21.tsv`'s `layered` on **18 of the 18** shared rows,
#     from a different tool and a different code path.
#   * `shipSten` and `shipTot` are byte-identical to `WIDEN-STENCIL-2026-08-22.tsv`'s `shipSten` and
#     `shipBytes` on **all 24 rows the two files share**, so the seam is measurably inert in published
#     bytes on two binaries, one with it compiled into `Flattener` and one without.
#   * columns 3-32 (the shape-term columns, which no widening touches) are byte-identical to
#     `WIDEN-STENCIL-2026-08-22.tsv` on those same **24** rows. ⚠️ The two share 24, not the 26 each
#     carries: this file has `Guilford_Psychometric Methods` p1 and `Ford_1941_Speech_` p3, the landed
#     file has `1954 - Why` p6 and p10. An earlier note put the overlap at "the same 27 rows"; it is 26
#     data rows each and 24 shared.
#   * `shipSten + shipBG + shipFG == shipTot`, and the same widened, on 26 of 26 rows.
#   * all 4 control pages read `wAdd` 0, `dTot` exactly 0 and `factor` 1.0000 — four determinism
#     controls, free.
# ⚠️ NOT re-run, and carried over from the stranded header rather than checked: `wStenAdd` was
# reproduced by ImageMagick on two pages (`Difference` of the two dumped stencils: 4,436 on Wilcox p2,
# 2,365 on Jones p7). Those two numbers do match this file's `wStenAdd`, but the dumped PNGs are not
# committed and the tool that wrote them is the rejected one, so this bullet is the one claim above that
# cannot be re-derived. The review of the diff that committed this file found it inside the "all re-run"
# list.
# ⚠️ `shrunkAsAllText` does not flip anywhere in this file, and neither does `backgroundWidth`, so
# `region`'s SECOND reader (`pageIsAllText()`'s comparand) changes no verdict on this population.
# ⚠️ Bytes are at the default Photo detail. ⚠️ These are sampled pages: scale with
# `Tools/stratify-corpus.py`, never by multiplication.
